_note: Quote of the day (/knowledge/quotes). Spanish-language quotations only, in their traditional wording with modern spelling, by authors who died before 1946, which puts them in the public domain under life+70 and under Spain's life+80 for authors who died before 1987. Every quote is a line from the author's own work and `source` names that work; `year` is the year of first publication or performance or, for a poem that circulated in manuscript, of writing. Lines known to be misattributed are left out on purpose (Ladran, Sancho…; Los muertos que vos matáis…; Venceréis, pero no convenceréis, whose wording is reconstructed). Verse line breaks are ' / ' (oneLine() in zitateData.js turns them into spaces). `disputed: true` would show a badge; no quote needs it. `meaning` says the quote in plain English (A2–B1). Word fields keep their old names: `de` is the Spanish word, `art` el or la. Written 2026-11-06. Wording and years were reviewed against what we know of the works, not against an edition; see the to-verify list in the culture report.

cervantes.name: Miguel de Cervantes
cervantes.bio: Cervantes wrote Don Quijote, often called the first modern novel. He was a soldier, was wounded in battle and spent five years as a captive in Algiers. He had little money for most of his life. Spanish is sometimes called “the language of Cervantes”.

manrique.name: Jorge Manrique
manrique.bio: Manrique was a nobleman and a soldier who died in battle. He is remembered for one long poem, written after the death of his father. It is about how life passes, and it is still read in Spanish schools.
manrique.kurz: A poet and soldier of the 15th century.

teresa.name: Teresa de Jesús
teresa.bio: Teresa was a Carmelite nun who founded many convents across Spain. She wrote about her life and faith in simple, lively Spanish. The Catholic Church made her a saint, and she is known in English as Teresa of Ávila.
teresa.kurz: A nun who wrote in lively, simple Spanish.

gracian.name: Baltasar Gracián
gracian.bio: Gracián was a Jesuit priest from Aragón. His short book of advice, the Oráculo manual, teaches how to live and deal with other people. His style is famous for saying a lot in very few words.
gracian.kurz: He wrote short, clever advice on how to live.

lope.name: Lope de Vega
lope.bio: Lope de Vega wrote hundreds of plays and helped to create the Spanish theatre of his time. He also wrote many poems. His private life was often as dramatic as his plays. People of his time called him a “monster of nature” because he wrote so much.

calderon.name: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
calderon.bio: Calderón was one of the great playwrights of the Spanish Golden Age. He studied, served as a soldier and later became a priest. His best-known play, La vida es sueño, asks whether life is real or a dream.
calderon.kurz: He wrote La vida es sueño.

quevedo.name: Francisco de Quevedo
quevedo.bio: Quevedo was a writer and a political adviser who spent time in prison. He wrote serious poems about love and death and very funny, sharp satire. He and the poet Góngora were famous enemies.
quevedo.kurz: A sharp, funny poet of the Golden Age.

gongora.name: Luis de Góngora
gongora.bio: Góngora was a priest and one of the great poets of the Golden Age. His long poems are famously difficult, but he also wrote short, simple songs. Poets of the 20th century, such as Lorca, admired him.

sorjuana.name: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
sorjuana.bio: Sor Juana grew up in New Spain, today Mexico, and taught herself much of what she knew. She became a nun so that she could study and write. She defended the right of women to learn. Her face is on Mexican money.
sorjuana.kurz: A Mexican poet who defended women’s right to learn.

larra.name: Mariano José de Larra
larra.bio: Larra was the sharpest journalist of his time in Spain. In his articles he made fun of bureaucracy, laziness and politics. He took his own life at 27, and many Spanish writers still see him as a model.
larra.kurz: A journalist who laughed at bureaucracy.

espronceda.name: José de Espronceda
espronceda.bio: Espronceda was a poet and political rebel who lived in exile for some years. He is the best-known Spanish Romantic poet after Bécquer. Many Spanish children still learn his poem about a pirate at school.
espronceda.kurz: He wrote the poem of the pirate.

zorrilla.name: José Zorrilla
zorrilla.bio: Zorrilla was a very popular Romantic writer. His play Don Juan Tenorio tells the old story of the great seducer. For many years, theatres in Spain performed it around 1 November, and some still do.
zorrilla.kurz: He wrote the play Don Juan Tenorio.

becquer.name: Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer
becquer.bio: Bécquer was a poet and journalist from Sevilla who died young and poor. His short love poems, the Rimas, came out after his death. They are simple and quiet, and they are among the most loved poems in Spanish.
becquer.kurz: He wrote short, simple love poems.

rosalia.name: Rosalía de Castro
rosalia.bio: Rosalía de Castro wrote in Galician and in Spanish. Her Galician book Cantares gallegos is a key work of that language. Her last book, in Spanish, is full of sadness and of the landscape of Galicia.

marti.name: José Martí
marti.bio: Martí was a Cuban writer and a leader in the fight for independence from Spain. He spent many years in exile, mostly in New York. He died in battle in Cuba. A famous song, Guantanamera, uses his verses.
marti.kurz: A Cuban poet and independence leader.

bolivar.name: Simón Bolívar
bolivar.bio: Bolívar led the wars of independence in much of northern South America. Bolivia takes its name from him. He hoped for one large union of the new countries, but it fell apart. People judge his politics in different ways.
bolivar.kurz: A leader of South American independence.

juarez.name: Benito Juárez
juarez.bio: Juárez was an Indigenous Zapotec who became a lawyer and president of Mexico. He separated Church and State and led the resistance to the French invasion. His birthday is a public holiday in Mexico.

hernandez.name: José Hernández
hernandez.bio: Hernández was an Argentine journalist and politician. His long poem Martín Fierro tells the story of a gaucho, a cowboy of the pampas, who is treated unfairly. It is a national classic in Argentina.
hernandez.kurz: He wrote the gaucho poem Martín Fierro.

dario.name: Rubén Darío
dario.bio: Darío was a Nicaraguan poet who lived in several countries, including Chile, Argentina, Spain and France. He led the movement called modernismo and changed the sound of poetry in Spanish on both sides of the Atlantic.
dario.kurz: A Nicaraguan poet who changed poetry in Spanish.

machado.name: Antonio Machado
machado.bio: Machado was a poet and a teacher of French in small Spanish towns. His poems speak about the land of Castile, time and memory. He left Spain at the end of the Civil War and died in France a few weeks later.
machado.kurz: A poet of Castile, time and memory.

unamuno.name: Miguel de Unamuno
unamuno.bio: Unamuno was a writer, a philosopher and the rector of the University of Salamanca. He wrote novels, poems and essays about faith, death and Spain. His opinions changed several times during his life, and they are still discussed.
unamuno.kurz: A writer and rector in Salamanca.

lorca.name: Federico García Lorca
lorca.bio: Lorca was a poet and playwright from a village near Granada. He wrote about love, death and the people of Andalucía. His plays, such as La casa de Bernarda Alba, are performed around the world. He was killed at the start of the Civil War.
lorca.kurz: A poet and playwright from Granada.

vallejo.name: César Vallejo
vallejo.bio: Vallejo was a Peruvian poet who moved to Paris in 1923 and never went back. His poems are about pain, poverty and solidarity, and their language is very much his own. He is seen as one of the great poets in Spanish of the 20th century.

storni.name: Alfonsina Storni
storni.bio: Storni was born in Switzerland and grew up in Argentina, where she worked as a teacher and a journalist. She raised a son alone at a time when this was hard for a woman. Her poems speak openly about the place of women in society.
storni.kurz: An Argentine poet who wrote about women’s lives.

quotes.author: calderon
quotes.text: ¿Qué es la vida? Un frenesí. / ¿Qué es la vida? Una ilusión, / una sombra, una ficción
quotes.source: La vida es sueño, Act II
quotes.meaning: Prince Segismundo wonders what life is. He says it is a madness, an illusion, a shadow, something invented.

words.hint: the dark shape something makes in the light

quotes.author: teresa
quotes.text: Entre los pucheros anda el Señor.
quotes.meaning: God is also there among the cooking pots. Even everyday work in the kitchen can be holy.

quotes.author: teresa
quotes.text: Nada te turbe, / nada te espante
quotes.meaning: Do not let anything worry you or frighten you. The poem goes on to say that God does not change.

quotes.author: calderon
quotes.text: que toda la vida es sueño, / y los sueños, sueños son.
quotes.source: La vida es sueño, Act II
quotes.meaning: All of life is a dream, and dreams are only dreams. So we cannot be sure what is real.

words.hint: the time from birth to death
what you see while you sleep

quotes.author: lope
quotes.text: Esto es amor: quien lo probó lo sabe.
quotes.meaning: The sonnet lists the strange feelings of love. Only people who have felt it know what it is like.

quotes.author: quevedo
quotes.text: Poderoso caballero / es don Dinero.
quotes.source: Letrilla “Madre, yo al oro me humillo”
quotes.meaning: Mr Money is a powerful gentleman. The poet is laughing at how money can buy almost anything.

quotes.author: gongora
quotes.text: Ándeme yo caliente / y ríase la gente.
quotes.meaning: As long as I am warm and comfortable, let people laugh. The poet prefers a simple life to what other people think.

words.hint: people in general; singular in Spanish

quotes.author: becquer
quotes.text: Por una mirada, un mundo; / por una sonrisa, un cielo
quotes.meaning: For one look from you, I would give the world; for one smile, I would give the heavens.

words.hint: the Earth and everyone on it
the happy shape of your mouth

quotes.author: zorrilla
quotes.text: ¿No es cierto, ángel de amor, / que en esta apartada orilla / más pura la luna brilla / y se respira mejor?
quotes.source: Don Juan Tenorio, Part I, Act IV
quotes.meaning: Don Juan speaks to the woman he loves. Isn’t it true, he asks, that the moon is brighter here, and the air is better?

words.hint: to give out or reflect light
to take air in and out

quotes.author: becquer
quotes.text: Poesía… eres tú.
quotes.meaning: She asks him what poetry is. He answers: poetry is you. One of the shortest and best-known love poems in Spanish.

words.hint: to be, for what someone or something is

quotes.author: marti
quotes.text: Yo soy un hombre sincero / de donde crece la palma
quotes.meaning: I am an honest man from the land where the palm tree grows, which means Cuba. The song Guantanamera made these words famous.

words.hint: a tall tree of hot countries

quotes.author: marti
quotes.text: Cultivo una rosa blanca / en junio como en enero
quotes.meaning: I grow a white rose in June as in January. The poet is kind all year round, to his friend and even to the person who hurts him.

words.hint: a flower, often red, with a sweet smell

quotes.author: cervantes
quotes.text: Donde una puerta se cierra, otra se abre.
quotes.meaning: When you lose one chance, another one often comes. It is an old saying, and Don Quijote uses it.

words.hint: what you open to go into a room

quotes.author: cervantes
quotes.text: Sábete, Sancho, que no es un hombre más que otro si no hace más que otro.
quotes.meaning: No person is better than another unless they do more than the other. Only your actions count.

words.hint: to know; here, an order: know this

quotes.author: espronceda
quotes.text: Con diez cañones por banda, / viento en popa, a toda vela
quotes.meaning: With ten cannons on each side and the wind behind it, the pirate’s ship moves at full speed. Viento en popa still means that things are going very well.

words.hint: a big old gun on a ship
the cloth that catches the wind on a boat

quotes.author: dario
quotes.text: La princesa está triste… ¿qué tendrá la princesa?
quotes.meaning: The princess is sad. What can be wrong with her? In Spanish the future tense, tendrá, here means “I wonder”.

words.hint: the daughter of a king or a queen

quotes.author: marti
quotes.text: Ser culto es el único modo de ser libre.
quotes.meaning: Being educated is the only way to be free. People who know things cannot be controlled so easily.

quotes.author: larra
quotes.text: Escribir en Madrid es llorar.
quotes.meaning: To write in Madrid is to cry. Larra felt that nobody was listening to writers in the Spain of his day.

words.hint: to have tears because you are sad

quotes.author: larra
quotes.text: Vuelva usted mañana.
quotes.source: Title of the article “Vuelva usted mañana”
quotes.meaning: Come back tomorrow. In this article an office keeps sending a visitor away. People in Spain still use the phrase to joke about bureaucracy.

quotes.author: bolivar
quotes.text: Moral y luces son nuestras primeras necesidades.
quotes.source: Speech at the Congress of Angostura
quotes.meaning: Good values and education are what the new countries need first. Luces, “lights”, here means knowledge.

words.hint: what lets you see; here, knowledge

quotes.author: cervantes
quotes.text: En un lugar de la Mancha, de cuyo nombre no quiero acordarme
quotes.meaning: This is the first line of the most famous novel in Spanish. The narrator says that the story starts in a village in La Mancha, and that he does not want to remember its name.

words.hint: to keep something in your memory

quotes.author: espronceda
quotes.text: que es mi barco mi tesoro, / que es mi dios la libertad
quotes.meaning: The pirate says that his ship is his treasure and that freedom is his god. For him nothing is worth more.

words.hint: gold and other things of great value

quotes.author: machado
quotes.text: Todo pasa y todo queda, / pero lo nuestro es pasar
quotes.source: Proverbios y cantares XLIV, in Campos de Castilla
quotes.meaning: Everything passes and everything stays, but what we do is pass. People and their lives are only here for a short time.

words.hint: a word that shows a contrast

quotes.author: machado
quotes.text: Mi infancia son recuerdos de un patio de Sevilla
quotes.meaning: My childhood is memories of a courtyard in Sevilla. The poet was born in a palace courtyard with a lemon tree, and he begins his self-portrait there.

words.hint: the time when you are a child
an open space inside a building

quotes.author: cervantes
quotes.text: Con la iglesia hemos dado, Sancho.
quotes.meaning: At night Don Quijote and Sancho walk into a church building. Today people use the phrase, often changed, when they run into a powerful institution.

words.hint: to find or run into something
you and I; here hidden in the verb: hemos

quotes.author: lorca
quotes.text: A las cinco de la tarde.
quotes.meaning: At five in the afternoon. It is the hour when the poet’s friend, a bullfighter, was fatally wounded. The line comes back again and again like a bell.

words.hint: the part of the day after lunch
here: used to say what time

quotes.author: rosalia
quotes.text: Dicen que no hablan las plantas, ni las fuentes, ni los pájaros
quotes.meaning: People say that plants, fountains and birds do not speak. The poet goes on to say that this is not true: for her, nature talks.

words.hint: a living thing that grows in the ground
a place where water comes out
an animal with feathers and wings

quotes.author: lorca
quotes.text: Verde que te quiero verde.
quotes.meaning: Green, how I love you, green. The line is not logical, and that is its power. It opens a dark, dreamlike poem.

quotes.author: hernandez
quotes.text: Los hermanos sean unidos, / porque esa es la ley primera
quotes.meaning: Brothers should stay together, because that is the first law. The old gaucho gives this advice to his sons.

words.hint: a son of the same parents

quotes.author: dario
quotes.text: Juventud, divino tesoro, / ¡ya te vas para no volver!
quotes.source: Canción de otoño en primavera, in Cantos de vida y esperanza
quotes.meaning: Youth, you wonderful treasure, you are leaving and you will not come back. The poet is getting older and looks back.

words.hint: the time when you are young

quotes.author: lope
quotes.text: ¿Quién mató al Comendador? / Fuenteovejuna, señor.
quotes.meaning: The people of a village kill a cruel lord. When the judge asks who did it, everyone gives the name of the village. Today the phrase means that a whole group acts together.

words.hint: a knight who ruled over land
a polite word for a man

quotes.author: sorjuana
quotes.text: Hombres necios que acusáis / a la mujer sin razón
quotes.meaning: Foolish men, you blame women without good reason. The poem says men criticise women for what men themselves ask of them.

words.hint: to say someone did something wrong

quotes.author: cervantes
quotes.text: La libertad, Sancho, es uno de los más preciosos dones que a los hombres dieron los cielos.
quotes.meaning: Don Quijote tells his friend Sancho that freedom is one of the best gifts people have ever received.

quotes.author: quevedo
quotes.text: polvo serán, mas polvo enamorado.
quotes.source: Sonnet “Amor constante más allá de la muerte”
quotes.meaning: After death, the lovers’ bodies will be dust, but dust that is still in love. Love is stronger than death.

words.hint: very small dry pieces of something
an old word for pero; note: no accent

quotes.author: gracian
quotes.text: Lo bueno, si breve, dos veces bueno.
quotes.source: Oráculo manual y arte de prudencia, 105
quotes.meaning: A good thing is twice as good if it is short. Say what you have to say and stop.

quotes.author: juarez
quotes.text: Entre los individuos, como entre las naciones, el respeto al derecho ajeno es la paz.
quotes.meaning: Between people, as between countries, peace means respecting the rights of others. Juárez said this after Mexico defeated the French invasion.

words.hint: something the law says you can have or do

quotes.author: storni
quotes.text: Tú me quieres alba, / me quieres de espumas
quotes.source: Tú me quieres blanca, in El dulce daño
quotes.meaning: You want me pure as the dawn, made of sea foam. The woman in the poem answers a man who asks her to be perfect, when he himself is not.

words.hint: dawn; feminine word, el because of the stressed a
the white bubbles on the sea

quotes.author: vallejo
quotes.text: Hay golpes en la vida, tan fuertes… ¡Yo no sé!
quotes.meaning: There are blows in life so hard that you have no words for them. The poet stops, because he does not know how to say it.

words.hint: the time from birth to death

quotes.author: cervantes
quotes.text: El que lee mucho y anda mucho, ve mucho y sabe mucho.
quotes.meaning: If you read a lot and travel a lot, you see many things and you learn a lot.

words.hint: to look at words and understand them

quotes.author: manrique
quotes.text: Nuestras vidas son los ríos / que van a dar en la mar, / que es el morir
quotes.source: Coplas a la muerte de su padre
quotes.meaning: Our lives are like rivers that flow into the sea, and the sea is death. All lives end in the same place.

words.hint: the time from birth to death
a large natural stream of water

quotes.author: cervantes
quotes.text: Cada uno es hijo de sus obras.
quotes.meaning: What you do makes you who you are. Your family name does not decide your worth.

words.hint: a male child of a parent

quotes.author: machado
quotes.text: Caminante, no hay camino, / se hace camino al andar.
quotes.source: Proverbios y cantares XXIX, in Campos de Castilla
quotes.meaning: Traveller, there is no path. You make the path by walking. Nobody can tell you exactly how to live your life.

words.hint: a person who walks a long way

quotes.author: becquer
quotes.text: Volverán las oscuras golondrinas
quotes.meaning: The dark swallows will come back. The birds will return next year, says the poet, but the love he has lost will not.

words.hint: a small bird that returns in spring

quotes.author: unamuno
quotes.text: La sangre de mi espíritu es mi lengua
quotes.source: Poem in Rosario de sonetos líricos
quotes.meaning: My language is the blood of my spirit. For Unamuno, his language is what keeps his inner life going.

words.hint: the red liquid in your body
the part of you that thinks and feels
